Let \(n=2024\) and let \(x\) be the number of interior nodes where four small rectangles meet. Counting the four corners of each small rectangle gives \(V=2n+2-x\) nodes. The nodes and fundamental segments form a connected planar graph whose faces are the \(n\) rectangles plus the outer face, so Euler’s formula \(V-E+(n+1)=2\) yields
\[
N=E=V+n-1=3n+1-x.
\]

Thus \(N\) is maximal when \(x=0\): \(N_{\max}=3n+1=6073\) (e.g. \(n\) parallel strips).

To minimize \(N\) we maximize \(x\). Refine any division by extending segments at T-junctions until every interior node is a cross; the result is an \(a\times b\) grid with \(ab\ge n\) and \((a-1)(b-1)\) crosses. Reversing one extension merges two rectangles and destroys at least one cross, so
\[
x\le (a-1)(b-1)-(ab-n)=n-a-b+1,
\]
hence \(N\ge 2n+a+b\) with \(ab\ge n\). The smallest possible \(a+b\) under \(ab\ge n\) is \(\lceil2\sqrt n\rceil=90\) (attained by \(44\times46\) or \(45\times45\)). Therefore
\[
N_{\min}=2n+90=4138.
\]

Finally \(N_{\max}+N_{\min}=6073+4138=10211\).

Let \(n=2024\).  Let \(V\) be the number of nodes, \(E=N\) the number of fundamental segments, and let \(X\) be the number of interior nodes where four rectangles meet (degree 4).  Counting corner incidences of the \(n\) rectangles gives \(4n=4+2V_b+3V_{T}+4X\), and Euler's formula \(V-E+(n+1)=2\) yields
\[
E=3n+1-X.
\]
Thus \(N\) is maximized when \(X=0\) (e.g. \(n-1\) parallel cuts), giving
\[
N_{\max}=3n+1.
\]
To minimize \(N\) we maximize \(X\).  If \(p\) distinct vertical and \(q\) distinct horizontal lines occur, then the partition is a coarsening of the \((p-1)\times(q-1)\) grid, so \(n\le (p-1)(q-1)\) and \(X\le (p-2)(q-2)\).  Optimizing gives
\[
X_{\max}=n-\lceil 2\sqrt n\rceil+1,\qquad N_{\min}=2n+\lceil 2\sqrt n\rceil.
\]
For \(n=2024\): \(\sqrt{2024}\approx44.99\), so \(\lceil2\sqrt{2024}\rceil=90\).  Hence
\[
N_{\max}=3\cdot2024+1=6073,\qquad N_{\min}=2\cdot2024+90=4138,
\]
and their sum is \(6073+4138=10211\).

Let \(V,N,n\) be the numbers of nodes, fundamental line segments and small rectangles (\(n=2024\)). The planar graph satisfies Euler’s formula \(V-N+(n+1)=2\), so \(N=V+n-1\).

Classify nodes: 4 corners (degree 2), \(b\) boundary non-corner nodes (degree 3), \(t\) interior T-junctions (degree 3), \(c\) interior crossings (degree 4). Summing degrees gives \(t+b+2c=2n-2\). Since \(V=t+c+b+4\), we get \(V=2n+2-c\) and therefore
\[N=3n+1-c.\]

Let \(s\) be the number of maximal interior segments. Each has two ends, which are boundary nodes or T-junctions, so \(b+t=2s\). Combining with the degree relation yields \(s+c=n-1\), hence
\[N=2n+2+s.\]

If there are \(v\) vertical and \(h\) horizontal maximal segments, then \(s=v+h\) and \(c\le vh\), so
\[n=1+c+s\le (v+1)(h+1)\le \Big\lfloor\frac{(s+2)^2}{4}\Big\rfloor.\]
Thus the minimal possible \(s\) is the smallest integer with \(\lfloor(s+2)^2/4\rfloor\ge n\). For \(n=2024\), \(89^2/4=1980.25\) and \(90^2/4=2025\), so \(s_{\min}=88\).

Maximum \(s=n-1\) occurs with no crossings (e.g. \(n-1\) parallel cuts), giving \(N_{\max}=3n+1=6073\). Minimum \(s=88\) gives \(N_{\min}=2n+2+88=4138\). Their sum is \(6073+4138=10211\).
